question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
She is the least reliablest person of all.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. least reliable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence contains a double superlative error — "least reliablest" wrongly combines the superlative marker "least" with the suffix "-est" on the same adjective.

• Rule — Degrees of Comparison: The superlative degree must be formed by only one method — either by adding "-est" to short (one or two syllable) adjectives, or by placing "most/least" before longer adjectives. Combining both on one adjective (e.g. "most best", "least worst", "least reliablest") is grammatically incorrect.
◦ Example: She is the most intelligent student in the class. (never "most intelligentest")

• "Reliable" is a three-syllable adjective, so its negative superlative must be formed with "least" alone, giving least reliable.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "leastest reliable" is incorrect because "leastest" is not a standard English word — it duplicates the superlative marker that "least" already supplies.

• Option 2: "less reliable" is incorrect because "less" is the comparative form, used to compare only two things, whereas "of all" signals comparison among three or more, which needs the superlative.

• Option 4: "lesser reliable" is incorrect for the same reason — "lesser" is a comparative form and cannot combine with "of all", which requires the superlative degree.

NOTE

• Comparative degree compares two persons/things and takes "-er"/"more"; superlative degree compares three or more and takes "-est"/"most" (or "least" for the negative superlative).

• Never double up the markers: avoid "more better", "most best", "least worst", "more easier", etc.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word 'Ravishing' from the given sentence.
The architect designed a stunning skyscraper with a sophisticated structural system.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Stunning.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Ravishing" means extremely beautiful, delightful, or attractive; capable of overwhelming someone with its beauty. (अत्यंत सुंदर, मनमोहक)
◦ Example: The bride looked ravishing in her wedding dress.

• In the given sentence, the word "stunning" (used to describe the skyscraper) carries the same sense of strikingly, overwhelmingly beautiful, making it the closest synonym of "ravishing" among the options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Sophisticated" (परिष्कृत): means refined, complex, or highly developed — it describes intricacy or refinement, not beauty.

• Option 2: "Skyscraper" (गगनचुंबी इमारत): is a noun meaning a very tall building; it is not a describing word at all, so it cannot be a synonym of an adjective like "ravishing".

• Option 4: "System" (प्रणाली): is a noun meaning an organised set of parts working together; it has no connection to beauty or attractiveness.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "ravishing": gorgeous, exquisite, breathtaking, stunning, enchanting.

• Do not confuse "ravishing" (beautiful) with "ravaging" (destroying) — the two words are commonly confused in SSC vocabulary questions.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.
The young artist spent countless hours perfecting her craft, trying with various methods
and mediums, and honing her creative vision until she had produced a stunning collection of works that showcased her unique talent and perspective.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. experimenting with different techniques.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined phrase "trying with various methods and mediums" describes an artist testing out different ways and materials to perfect her craft — this is precisely what "experimenting with different techniques" means. (विभिन्न तकनीकों के साथ प्रयोग करना)
◦ Example: The chef spent years experimenting with different techniques before perfecting the recipe.

• "Methods and mediums" (the ways and materials used to create art) is best replaced by "techniques", and "trying" is best replaced by "experimenting", since both phrases describe deliberate trial to improve a craft.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "exploring with different factors" is incorrect because "factors" refers to causes or elements influencing an outcome, not artistic methods or materials — it does not fit the context of perfecting a craft.

• Option 3: "merging with different variations" is incorrect because "merging" means combining or blending things together, whereas the sentence describes trying out separate methods, not combining them.

• Option 4: "researching with different types" is incorrect because "researching" suggests theoretical investigation or study, not the hands-on, practical trial-and-error implied by "trying with various methods".

NOTE

• In phrase-substitution questions, focus on matching the exact sense of the underlined words, not just similar-sounding or loosely related words.

• Commonly confused pairs in such questions: experiment vs. explore vs. research vs. investigate — each has a distinct nuance.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Calendr.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Calendar", not "Calendr". The word ends in -endar, not -endr.

• Spelling key: CAL + END + AR. Remember it as a chart showing the days, weeks, and months of the year — "calendAR" has an "a" before the final "r", which the given option "Calendr" wrongly drops.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Conscientious" is correctly spelt — meaning careful and diligent in one's duty.

• Option 3: "Colleague" is correctly spelt — meaning a fellow worker.

• Option 4: "Conspicuous" is correctly spelt — meaning easily noticeable.

NOTE

• Words ending in "-ar" that are often misspelt as "-er" or with dropped vowels: calendar, grammar, similar, familiar, particular, popular.

• Always sound out a suspected word syllable by syllable (CAL-EN-DAR) to catch a missing letter.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
By whom was this poem written?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Who wrote this poem?

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "By whom was this poem written?" is an interrogative sentence in the Simple Past Tense (Passive Voice).

• Rule — Simple Past Tense (Interrogative, Wh-word as subject/agent):
◦ Passive: By + whom + was/were + Object + V3?
◦ Active: Who + V2 + Object?

• Applying the rule: "by whom" becomes the interrogative subject "who"; the object "this poem" becomes the object of the active sentence; and the past participle "written" becomes the simple past form "wrote".
◦ Active: Who wrote this poem?

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "had wrote" is an ungrammatical mix of the past perfect auxiliary "had" with the simple past form "wrote" instead of the past participle "written"; it does not match the simple past tense of the original.

• Option 2 is incorrect because "has written" is the active form of the Present Perfect Tense, whereas the original sentence is in the Simple Past Tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "writes" is the active form of the Simple Present Tense, not the Simple Past Tense required here.

NOTE

• When the passive sentence begins with "By whom", the active version always begins with the interrogative pronoun "Who" acting as the subject.

• Tense must be preserved exactly when converting between voices — only the sentence structure and the form of the verb change, not the tense itself.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined segment in the following sentence.
Everything in the mansion was in great confusion after the robbery.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Pell-mell.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Pell-mell" means in a confused, disorderly, or hurried manner; utter chaos or disarray, and matches the underlined segment "great confusion" exactly. (अस्त-व्यस्त, अफरा-तफरी में)
◦ Example: After the fire alarm rang, the students rushed pell-mell out of the classroom.

• The mansion, after being robbed, would naturally be left in a state of complete disorder — everything thrown about in confusion — which is the essence of "pell-mell".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Pick holes" (दोष निकालना): means to find fault with something or criticise minor details.
◦ Example: The critic always tries to pick holes in every new film.

• Option 3: "Turn over a new leaf" (नया जीवन शुरू करना): means to start behaving in a better way than before; to make a fresh start.

• Option 4: "Damp squib" (असफल प्रयास): means an event or effort that turns out to be a complete failure or disappointment despite high expectations.

NOTE

• Other idioms of disorder/chaos often asked in SSC: "At sixes and sevens", "In a mess", "Topsy-turvy" (all meaning disorganised or confused).

• Do not confuse "pell-mell" (disorder) with "helter-skelter" (in a hurried, disorganised manner) — both are close synonyms and sometimes appear as distractors together.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined word in the following sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution required'.
The students were restored to complete the assignment by Friday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. expected.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "restored" means brought back to a previous good condition or position, which makes no sense in the context of students completing an assignment by a deadline. (पुनर्स्थापित करना)

• The correct word here is "expected", meaning required or supposed to do something, which fits the meaning: the students were required/supposed to complete the assignment by Friday. (अपेक्षित होना)
◦ Example: The employees were expected to submit their reports by the end of the day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "declared" is incorrect because "declared" means formally or officially announced something, which does not fit the sense of an obligation to complete an assignment.

• Option 3: "designed" is incorrect because "designed" means planned or created for a specific purpose; it does not convey the idea of an expectation or requirement placed on the students.

• Option 4: "No substitution required" is incorrect because "restored" is clearly the wrong word in this context and must be substituted with a word that conveys obligation, such as "expected".

NOTE

• Such questions test contextual word usage — always check whether the underlined word logically fits the rest of the sentence before deciding no substitution is needed.

• Commonly confused near-homophones/near-synonyms in SSC: restored vs. expected vs. required vs. requested — each carries a distinct meaning.

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
There was a sudden esklation of violent acts which led to the starting of the second world war.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Esklation.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "Escalation", not "Esklation". The word uses the letters "sc" (pronounced like "sk"), not the letter combination "skl".

• Spelling key: ES + CAL + ATION. The word comes from escalate, meaning to increase in intensity or extent. "Esklation" wrongly replaces "sc" with "skl".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "Starting" is correctly spelt.

• Option 3: "Violent" is correctly spelt.

• Option 4: "Sudden" is correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Words with the "sc" sounding like "sk" that are commonly misspelt: escalate, scheme, scholar, discipline, muscle.

• The related noun form is "escalation" and the verb is "escalate" — both frequently tested in SSC spelling and vocabulary questions.

question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.
P. a man in a maroon colour flannel shirt
Q. rounded a corner and walked into the middle of the main street of Yellow Sky
R. which had been purchased for purposes of decoration
S. and made principally by some Jewish women on the East side of New York
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. PRSQ.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Part P — "a man in a maroon colour flannel shirt" — introduces the subject of the sentence and must come first.

• Part R — "which had been purchased for purposes of decoration" — is a relative clause beginning with "which", and it must immediately follow the noun it describes (the shirt in P), since a relative clause modifies the noun right before it.

• Part S — "and made principally by some Jewish women on the East side of New York" — continues the same relative clause with "and", so it must directly follow R (both R and S describe the shirt: where it was bought, and by whom it was made).

• Part Q — "rounded a corner and walked into the middle of the main street of Yellow Sky" — is the main verb clause describing the man's action, and logically comes last, after the descriptive clause about his shirt is complete.

• Combining them: "A man in a maroon colour flannel shirt, which had been purchased for purposes of decoration and made principally by some Jewish women on the East side of New York, rounded a corner and walked into the middle of the main street of Yellow Sky." This reads as a complete, meaningful sentence, confirming the order P-R-S-Q.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: PRQS is incorrect because it places Q (the main action) before S, breaking the continuous relative clause R–S that must stay together.

• Option 3: PSRQ is incorrect because it places S before R, but S begins with "and", meaning it must continue R, not precede it.

• Option 4: PQRS is incorrect because it inserts the main clause Q immediately after P, before the descriptive relative clause R–S about the shirt is complete, breaking the logical flow.

NOTE

• In para-jumble questions, always locate the part with the subject/main noun first, then trace connector words like "which", "and", "but" to link dependent clauses in the correct sequence.

• A clause beginning with "and" almost always continues the clause immediately preceding it rather than starting a new idea.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
He wore a bizarre outfit for the party.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Weird.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Bizarre" means very strange, odd, or unusual, especially in a striking or unexpected way. (विचित्र, अजीब)
◦ Example: The scientists reported a bizarre phenomenon that no one could explain.

• "Weird" carries the same sense of strangeness or oddity, making it the most appropriate synonym among the given options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Normal" (सामान्य): means conforming to a standard or usual type — the direct opposite of "bizarre".

• Option 2: "Usual" (सामान्य, प्रचलित): means habitually occurring or done; commonly expected — also opposite in sense to "bizarre".

• Option 4: "Familiar" (परिचित): means well-known or easily recognised — again opposite to the sense of strangeness conveyed by "bizarre".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "bizarre": strange, peculiar, eccentric, odd, curious, outlandish.

• Antonym of "bizarre": normal, ordinary, conventional, usual — useful to remember since SSC often sets antonym-style distractors as options in synonym questions.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.
She detests capsicum so much that she would prefer going empty stomach.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. loathes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Detests" means feels intense dislike or hatred for something. (घृणा करना, नफरत करना)
◦ Example: He detests dishonesty in any form.

• "Loathes" carries the exact same meaning — an intense feeling of dislike or disgust — making it the correct synonym.
◦ Example: She loathes waking up early in the morning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "prompts" (प्रेरित करना): means causes or encourages someone to do something; unrelated to dislike.

• Option 2: "marvels" (आश्चर्यचकित होना): means feels great wonder or admiration — the opposite sense of "detests".

• Option 3: "rebels" (विद्रोह करना): means resists or fights against authority or a rule; it does not carry the sense of personal dislike for a thing like capsicum.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "detest": abhor, despise, hate, loathe, abominate.

• Antonym of "detest": adore, love, admire, cherish — often used as distractors in such synonym questions.

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom for the underlined words in the given sentence.
He was alone and knew the dangers ahead during his journey, but he tried to keep up
his confidence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. whistled in the dark.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "Whistled in the dark" means to try to appear brave or confident in a frightening or difficult situation, despite feeling afraid, which exactly matches the underlined phrase "tried to keep up his confidence". (डर के बावजूद हिम्मत दिखाने की कोशिश करना)
◦ Example: Despite the looming exam, he kept whistling in the dark, telling everyone he wasn't worried.

• The context of the sentence — a man alone, aware of dangers ahead, yet trying to stay confident — perfectly fits this idiom's meaning of putting on a brave face despite fear.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "made a sterner stuff": not a standard English idiom in this form (the correct expression is "made of sterner stuff", meaning to have a strong, resilient character), and it does not fit the grammar or sense of the sentence here.

• Option 3: "stepped up his game" (अपने प्रदर्शन में सुधार करना): means to improve one's performance or effort, which is not the same as trying to appear confident despite fear.

• Option 4: "wouldn't be caught dead" (किसी भी हालत में नहीं करना): means to never want to be seen doing something or in some situation; unrelated to putting on a brave face.

NOTE

• Other idioms about courage/confidence often asked in SSC: "Keep a stiff upper lip" (remain stoic/unemotional in adversity), "Face the music" (accept consequences bravely), "Put up a brave front".

• "Made of sterner stuff" (a related but different idiom) means having a strong and resilient character — do not confuse it with "whistled in the dark".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Timid
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Nervous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Timid" means showing a lack of courage or confidence; easily frightened, shy, or apprehensive. (डरपोक, संकोची)
◦ Example: The timid child hid behind his mother when strangers approached.

• Among the given options, "Nervous" (feeling anxious, apprehensive, or easily agitated) is closest in sense to "timid", since both describe a lack of confidence or ease in a situation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Magical" (जादुई): means having supernatural or enchanting qualities; entirely unrelated to "timid".

• Option 2: "Honest" (ईमानदार): means truthful and sincere; describes moral character, not fearfulness.

• Option 3: "Fearless" (निडर): means having no fear; this is actually the antonym of "timid", not its synonym.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "timid": shy, meek, diffident, apprehensive, timorous.

• Antonym of "timid": bold, fearless, courageous, audacious — such antonym-style words are frequently placed as distractors in synonym questions, so always check the exact sense required.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.
This route cannot get more ____________ (simplified) than it already is.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. convoluted.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Simplified" means made easier to understand or do; made less complex. (सरल बनाया गया)

• The antonym required is "Convoluted", meaning extremely complex, intricate, or difficult to follow; twisted and complicated. (जटिल, उलझा हुआ)
◦ Example: The plot of the novel was so convoluted that readers struggled to follow the storyline.

• The sentence implies the route is already at its highest degree of simplicity, and the blank (paired with "more") logically calls for the opposite idea — that it cannot become more complicated/convoluted than it already is (in the sense that it is already extremely complex) — matching the antonym relationship the question demands.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "uniform" (एकसमान): means consistent or unvarying in form; it is not an antonym of "simplified".

• Option 3: "homogenous" (सजातीय): means composed of similar or identical parts; unrelated to the idea of complexity versus simplicity.

• Option 4: "unvaried" (अपरिवर्तित): means not changing or lacking variety; this is not opposite in meaning to "simplified" either.

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "convoluted": complicated, intricate, complex, tangled, elaborate.

• Antonym-type fill-in-the-blank questions require first identifying the exact meaning of the bracketed word, and then choosing the option that expresses its precise opposite — not merely an unrelated or vaguely different word.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.
A particular form of a language which is peculiar to a specific region or social group.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Dialect.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Dialect" is a particular form of a language which is specific to a particular region or social group, differing from the standard language in vocabulary, grammar, or pronunciation. (क्षेत्रीय बोली)
◦ Example: The novel was written in the Yorkshire dialect, full of local expressions.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Singular" (एकवचन): in grammar, refers to a form denoting only one person or thing; it has nothing to do with regional forms of language.

• Option 2: "Slang" (अनौपचारिक भाषा): refers to very informal words and phrases used typically among particular groups of people (e.g., friends, a profession), often more casual/temporary than a regionally rooted dialect, and not tied specifically to a region.

• Option 4: "Referendum" (जनमत संग्रह): means a general vote by the electorate on a single political question; entirely unrelated to language.

NOTE

• Other commonly asked one-word substitutes related to language: "Vernacular" (the native language of a region/country), "Lingua franca" (a common language used between speakers of different native languages), "Jargon" (specialised terminology used within a particular trade or profession).

• Do not confuse "dialect" (a regional/social variant of a language) with "accent" (a distinctive way of pronouncing words).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.
Varun is handsome than his brother.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. more handsome than.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence compares two people — Varun and his brother — which requires the comparative degree, not the positive or superlative degree.

• Rule — Comparative Degree: For adjectives of two or more syllables (such as "handsome"), the comparative is formed by placing "more" before the adjective, and the comparison is completed with the conjunction "than" (never "to").
◦ Structure: Subject + is/are + more + adjective + than + Object.

• Applying the rule: "handsome" becomes "more handsome", and it must be followed by "than", giving "more handsome than".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "much handsome to" is incorrect because "much" cannot directly modify the positive form of a multi-syllable adjective in a comparison, and "to" is the wrong conjunction (it should be "than").

• Option 2: "most handsome than" is incorrect because "most" is used for the superlative degree (comparing three or more), not the comparative degree needed when comparing only two people.

• Option 4: "more handsome to" is incorrect because, although "more handsome" correctly forms the comparative, it must be followed by "than", not "to".

NOTE

• The conjunction "than" is always used with the comparative degree (e.g., taller than, more beautiful than); never use "then" or "to" in its place.

• Comparative forms: short adjectives take "-er" (taller), while adjectives of two or more syllables generally take "more" (more handsome, more intelligent).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The GDP of the country has growth rapidly since independence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. has grown rapidly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence uses the time marker "since independence", which signals an action that started in the past and continues up to (or is relevant to) the present — this requires the Present Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense:
◦ Structure: Subject + has/have + V3 (past participle) + ...
◦ "Since" (a point of time in the past) and "for" (a duration) are typical markers of the Present Perfect (or Present Perfect Continuous) tense.

• Applying the rule: the subject "The GDP" is singular/third person, so the auxiliary is "has"; the verb "grow" must be in its past participle form "grown", giving "has grown rapidly".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "had been grow rapidly" is incorrect because it mixes the past perfect continuous auxiliary "had been" with the base form "grow" instead of the "-ing" form; it also wrongly uses the past perfect tense, which is not indicated here.

• Option 3: "have grown been rapidly" is incorrect because "have" does not agree with the singular subject "The GDP" (which requires "has"), and the word order "grown been" is ungrammatical.

• Option 4: "had grow rapidly" is incorrect because "had" (past perfect) is the wrong tense for "since independence", and "grow" should be the past participle "grown", not the base form.

NOTE

• "Since" is always followed by a specific point of time (since independence, since 2010, since Monday), while "for" is followed by a duration (for five years, for a long time) — both typically pair with perfect tenses.

• Common irregular past participles tested by SSC: grow–grew–grown, write–wrote–written, break–broke–broken, speak–spoke–spoken.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The letter was written by the author and mailed to the publisher.
option_1: The letter was written and mailed to the publisher by the author.
option_2: The author wrote the letter and mailed it to the publisher.
option_3: The publisher received the letter written by the author.
option_4: The letter was being written by the author and mailed to the publisher.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The author wrote the letter and mailed it to the publisher.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The letter was written by the author and mailed to the publisher" is a compound sentence in the Simple Past Tense (Passive Voice), containing two actions performed by the same subject (the author): writing the letter and mailing it.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the agent "the author" becomes the subject; "the letter" becomes the object (referred to as "it" the second time to avoid repetition); "written" becomes "wrote" and "mailed" becomes "mailed" (same form for regular verb in active past).
◦ Active: The author wrote the letter and mailed it to the publisher.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it remains entirely in the passive voice ("was written and mailed... by the author"), it does not convert the sentence to active voice at all.

• Option 3 is incorrect because it changes the meaning and subject of the sentence — the original describes the author's actions, not the publisher receiving the letter, and it does not preserve both actions (writing and mailing) performed by the author.

• Option 4 is incorrect because it also stays in the passive voice ("was being written... by the author") and additionally shifts the tense incorrectly to the past continuous passive, which does not match the original simple past tense.

NOTE

• When a passive sentence contains two verbs joined by "and" sharing the same subject/agent, both verbs must be converted to active voice and can share the same active subject.

• Always replace a repeated object noun with an appropriate pronoun ("it", "them") in the second clause of the active sentence, exactly as done here with "it" for "the letter".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.
Proposal
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Scheme.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "Proposal" means a plan or suggestion put forward for consideration or discussion. (प्रस्ताव, योजना)
◦ Example: The committee accepted the manager's proposal to extend the office hours.

• "Scheme" also means a formal plan or arrangement for achieving a particular purpose, making it the closest synonym of "proposal" among the given options.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Filling" (भरना): refers to a substance used to fill something, or the act of filling; unrelated to the idea of a plan or suggestion.

• Option 3: "Refusal" (अस्वीकृति): means the act of declining or rejecting something — this is roughly opposite to accepting/putting forward a plan, not a synonym of "proposal".

• Option 4: "Addition" (जोड़): means the act of adding something, or something added; unrelated in meaning to "proposal".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "proposal": suggestion, plan, project, offer, proposition.

• "Proposal" can also specifically mean an offer of marriage — context determines which sense is intended, but the general/plan sense is what is tested here.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
The politician used a/an mild and indirect word to describe the controversial policy, in order to soften the blow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. euphemism.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Euphemism" is a mild, indirect, or vague word or expression substituted for one considered to be too harsh, blunt, or offensive, which exactly matches the underlined phrase "mild and indirect word". (शब्दों को मृदु/सौम्य रूप में प्रयोग करना)
◦ Example: "Passed away" is a euphemism for "died"; "downsizing" is a euphemism for "laying off employees".

• The sentence explicitly states the politician wanted "to soften the blow" while describing a controversial policy — this is the exact purpose a euphemism serves.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "oxymoron" (विरोधाभासी शब्द-युग्म): a figure of speech that combines two contradictory terms (e.g., "deafening silence"); it does not mean a mild/softened expression.

• Option 2: "metaphor" (रूपक): a figure of speech that describes something by directly referring to it as another thing to suggest a resemblance (e.g., "time is money"); it does not necessarily soften harsh meaning.

• Option 4: "hyperbole" (अतिशयोक्ति): a figure of speech using deliberate exaggeration for emphasis (e.g., "I've told you a million times"); this is the opposite effect of softening — it intensifies rather than mutes meaning.

NOTE

• Other commonly tested figures of speech: simile (comparison using "like"/"as"), irony (saying the opposite of what is meant), personification (giving human qualities to non-human things), litotes (understatement using a negative, e.g., "not bad" for "good").

• Euphemisms are frequently used in formal, political, or sensitive contexts to avoid causing offence or discomfort.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

India will host an international summit on Buddhism here on April 20 and 21. Delegates from 30 countries will participate, a notable exception (1) ________ China. Tibetan spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, is also unlikely to attend the two-day conclave.
The maiden conference being organised by the Union Culture Ministry and the International Buddhist Confederation will discuss (2) ________ global issues through a Buddhist perspective.
Over 170 delegates from countries such as Mexico, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand and Japan and 150 from India will participate in the summit to be held in the national capital. The delegates (3) ________ prominent scholars, monks, diplomats and members of Buddhist organisations across the globe. The largest number of delegates are from Sri Lanka (20) and Vietnam (30).
Abhijit Haldar, Director General of International Buddhist Confederation, said that while no delegate had been confirmed from China, there would be two participants from Taiwan.
“The invitations (4) ________ sent to various Buddhist institutions and not to governments,” Mr. Haldar added. He also mentioned that the Dalai Lama (5) ________ not attend the event due to health issues.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. being.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "Delegates from 30 countries will participate, a notable exception ________ China." Here, the clause "a notable exception being China" is a participle (non-finite) clause that adds extra information about the main clause, without needing its own main verb and subject-verb agreement.

• Rule — Present Participle ("-ing" form) in absolute/participial constructions: When a phrase is added to a sentence to give additional information without a connecting conjunction, the "-ing" form (present participle) of "to be" — i.e. "being" — is used to smoothly attach it to the main clause.
◦ Example: The team won every match, a remarkable feat being achieved for the first time.

• Applying the rule: "a notable exception being China" grammatically and smoothly extends the idea that all countries except China are participating.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "been" is incorrect because "been" is the past participle of "to be" and requires an auxiliary verb (has/have/had) before it to function correctly; it cannot be used alone to introduce this appositive-like clause.

• Option 3: "be" is incorrect because the base form "be" needs a modal or "to" before it (e.g., "will be", "to be") and cannot directly follow a noun phrase like "a notable exception" without one.

• Option 4: "are" is incorrect because "are" is a finite verb form requiring a plural subject with proper subject-verb agreement and would create a run-on/comma-splice sentence when simply inserted here without a connecting conjunction.

NOTE

• Non-finite "-ing" clauses (participial phrases) are common in formal/journalistic writing to add extra descriptive information smoothly without starting a new independent clause.

• Distinguish carefully between "being" (present participle, ongoing/descriptive), "been" (past participle, needs an auxiliary), and "be" (base form, needs a modal/to).

Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

India will host an international summit on Buddhism here on April 20 and 21. Delegates from 30 countries will participate, a notable exception (1) ________ China. Tibetan spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, is also unlikely to attend the two-day conclave.
The maiden conference being organised by the Union Culture Ministry and the International Buddhist Confederation will discuss (2) ________ global issues through a Buddhist perspective.
Over 170 delegates from countries such as Mexico, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand and Japan and 150 from India will participate in the summit to be held in the national capital. The delegates (3) ________ prominent scholars, monks, diplomats and members of Buddhist organisations across the globe. The largest number of delegates are from Sri Lanka (20) and Vietnam (30).
Abhijit Haldar, Director General of International Buddhist Confederation, said that while no delegate had been confirmed from China, there would be two participants from Taiwan.
“The invitations (4) ________ sent to various Buddhist institutions and not to governments,” Mr. Haldar added. He also mentioned that the Dalai Lama (5) ________ not attend the event due to health issues.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. contemporary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "...will discuss ________ global issues through a Buddhist perspective." This refers to a modern international summit discussing present-day, current global issues, which requires the word "contemporary", meaning belonging to or occurring in the present time; modern.

• A summit held in the current year would logically address issues relevant to today's world, not issues from the past — confirming that "contemporary" fits best, contextually as well as logically.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "classical" refers to something from a traditional, historically established, or ancient standard (e.g., classical music, classical literature); it does not describe present-day global issues.

• Option 3: "old" simply means having existed for a long time; while not entirely nonsensical, it lacks the precise sense of "present-day/current" that the context of an international summit requires, and is a weaker, less exam-appropriate fit than "contemporary".

• Option 4: "ancient" means belonging to the very distant past; this directly contradicts the context of a modern summit discussing present-time issues.

NOTE

• "Contemporary" has two related senses: (1) belonging to the present time, and (2) existing or occurring at the same time as something else — both senses are commonly tested in SSC vocabulary/cloze questions.

• Word pairs often confused with "contemporary": modern (relating to the present or recent times in general) vs. contemporary (specifically of the current period, or coexisting in time).

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

India will host an international summit on Buddhism here on April 20 and 21. Delegates from 30 countries will participate, a notable exception (1) ________ China. Tibetan spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, is also unlikely to attend the two-day conclave.
The maiden conference being organised by the Union Culture Ministry and the International Buddhist Confederation will discuss (2) ________ global issues through a Buddhist perspective.
Over 170 delegates from countries such as Mexico, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand and Japan and 150 from India will participate in the summit to be held in the national capital. The delegates (3) ________ prominent scholars, monks, diplomats and members of Buddhist organisations across the globe. The largest number of delegates are from Sri Lanka (20) and Vietnam (30).
Abhijit Haldar, Director General of International Buddhist Confederation, said that while no delegate had been confirmed from China, there would be two participants from Taiwan.
“The invitations (4) ________ sent to various Buddhist institutions and not to governments,” Mr. Haldar added. He also mentioned that the Dalai Lama (5) ________ not attend the event due to health issues.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. include.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "The delegates ________ prominent scholars, monks, diplomats and members of Buddhist organisations across the globe." The subject of this sentence is "The delegates", which is a plural noun.

• Rule — Subject-Verb Agreement (Simple Present Tense): A plural subject takes the base form of the verb (without "-s"/"-es") in the simple present tense.
◦ Structure: Plural Subject + V1 (base form) + Object.

• Applying the rule: since "delegates" is plural, the verb must be the base form "include", not "includes" (singular form).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "included" is incorrect because it is the past tense/past participle form, which does not fit the passage's overall present-tense, factual/descriptive style used to describe who the delegates are.

• Option 3: "including" is incorrect because the "-ing" form cannot function as the main finite verb of the clause on its own; it would leave the sentence without a proper verb.

• Option 4: "includes" is incorrect because "includes" is the singular present-tense form (used with he/she/it or a singular subject), but here the subject "the delegates" is plural.

NOTE

• A plural subject always takes the base (V1) form of the verb in the simple present tense; only a third-person singular subject takes the "-s/-es" ending.

• Always identify the true grammatical subject of the clause before choosing the verb form, especially in passages with multiple nouns nearby that could be mistaken for the subject.

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

India will host an international summit on Buddhism here on April 20 and 21. Delegates from 30 countries will participate, a notable exception (1) ________ China. Tibetan spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, is also unlikely to attend the two-day conclave.
The maiden conference being organised by the Union Culture Ministry and the International Buddhist Confederation will discuss (2) ________ global issues through a Buddhist perspective.
Over 170 delegates from countries such as Mexico, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand and Japan and 150 from India will participate in the summit to be held in the national capital. The delegates (3) ________ prominent scholars, monks, diplomats and members of Buddhist organisations across the globe. The largest number of delegates are from Sri Lanka (20) and Vietnam (30).
Abhijit Haldar, Director General of International Buddhist Confederation, said that while no delegate had been confirmed from China, there would be two participants from Taiwan.
“The invitations (4) ________ sent to various Buddhist institutions and not to governments,” Mr. Haldar added. He also mentioned that the Dalai Lama (5) ________ not attend the event due to health issues.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. were.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "The invitations ________ sent to various Buddhist institutions and not to governments." This is a passive voice construction in the Simple Past Tense, and the subject "invitations" is plural.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense (Passive Voice):
◦ Structure: Subject + was/were + V3 (past participle) + ...
◦ A plural subject takes the auxiliary "were"; a singular subject takes "was".

• Applying the rule: since "invitations" is plural and the past participle "sent" is already provided, the correct auxiliary is "were", giving "The invitations were sent...".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "had" is incorrect because "had" would require the past participle to follow directly to form the past perfect active (e.g., "had sent"), but here the sense required is passive ("were sent"), and "had" also does not fit the plural passive construction being tested.

• Option 3: "has" is incorrect because "has" is a present-tense auxiliary used with singular subjects (has sent), which agrees with neither the plural subject "invitations" nor the past-tense context of the passage.

• Option 4: "was" is incorrect because "was" is the singular past-tense auxiliary, but "invitations" is plural and therefore requires "were".

NOTE

• In passive voice, the auxiliary "be" (is/am/are/was/were) must always agree in number with the grammatical subject, regardless of the number of the underlying "doer" of the action.

• Passive voice formula recap: Object (as new subject) + was/were + V3 + (by + agent).

question:
Comprehension:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

India will host an international summit on Buddhism here on April 20 and 21. Delegates from 30 countries will participate, a notable exception (1) ________ China. Tibetan spiritual leader, the Dalai Lama, is also unlikely to attend the two-day conclave.
The maiden conference being organised by the Union Culture Ministry and the International Buddhist Confederation will discuss (2) ________ global issues through a Buddhist perspective.
Over 170 delegates from countries such as Mexico, Cambodia, Laos, Thailand and Japan and 150 from India will participate in the summit to be held in the national capital. The delegates (3) ________ prominent scholars, monks, diplomats and members of Buddhist organisations across the globe. The largest number of delegates are from Sri Lanka (20) and Vietnam (30).
Abhijit Haldar, Director General of International Buddhist Confederation, said that while no delegate had been confirmed from China, there would be two participants from Taiwan.
“The invitations (4) ________ sent to various Buddhist institutions and not to governments,” Mr. Haldar added. He also mentioned that the Dalai Lama (5) ________ not attend the event due to health issues.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. might.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: "He also mentioned that the Dalai Lama ________ not attend the event due to health issues." This expresses a possibility — that the Dalai Lama may or may not attend, due to his health — not a certainty, obligation, or past habit.

• Rule — Modal verb "might": "Might" is used to express a weak possibility or uncertainty about a future action, which is exactly the sense conveyed here regarding the Dalai Lama's uncertain attendance because of health issues.
◦ Example: She might not come to the party if she is unwell.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "ought to" is incorrect because it expresses moral obligation or duty/advisability (something that should be done), not mere possibility due to health reasons.

• Option 3: "used to" is incorrect because it expresses a past habitual action that no longer happens, which does not fit the context of a future/uncertain event (the upcoming summit).

• Option 4: "dare" is incorrect because it expresses courage or boldness to do something risky, which is unrelated to the sense of possibility due to poor health.

NOTE

• Modals of possibility, in increasing order of certainty: might/may (weak possibility) < could (possibility/ability) < should (likelihood/expectation) < must (near certainty).

• "Might" is also used as the past tense of "may" in reported speech, and to indicate a more tentative/polite possibility than "may" in modern usage.
